classification.difficultyReason: Factor the symbolic derivative and distinguish the universal stationary root from endpoint roots that exist only when the corresponding exponent exceeds one.

content.prompt: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers, and let $$f(x)=x^m(x-1)^n.$$ Find the value(s) of $x$ when the tangents are horizontal.

answer.short:
$x=\dfrac{m}{m+n}$; also $x=0$ if $m>1$, and $x=1$ if $n>1$.

Factor $f'(x)$ and retain zeros only when their corresponding factor has a positive exponent.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=mx^{m-1}(x-1)^n+nx^m(x-1)^{n-1}\\f'(x)&=x^{m-1}(x-1)^{n-1}[m(x-1)+nx]\\f'(x)&=x^{m-1}(x-1)^{n-1}[(m+n)x-m].\end{align*}$$

 Hence $f'(x)=0$ at $x=\dfrac{m}{m+n}$. The factor $x^{m-1}$ also gives $x=0$ when $m>1$; the factor $(x-1)^{n-1}$ also gives $x=1$ when $n>1$.
